studies.title: Facial expressiveness and physiological arousal in frontotemporal dementia: Phenotypic clinical profiles and neural correlates.
studies.abstract: Early theories of emotion processing propose an interplay between autonomic function and cognitive appraisal of emotions. Patients with frontotemporal dementia show profound social cognition deficits and atrophy in regions implicated in autonomic emotional responses (insula, amygdala, prefrontal cortex), yet objective measures of facial expressiveness and physiological arousal have been relatively unexplored. We investigated psychophysiological responses (surface facial electromyography (EMG); skin conductance level (SCL)) to emotional stimuli in 25 behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) patients, 14 semantic dementia (SD) patients, and 24 healthy older controls, while viewing emotionally positive, neutral, or negative video clips. Voxel-based morphometry was conducted to identify neural correlates of responses. Unlike controls, patients with bvFTD did not show differential facial EMG responses according to emotion condition, whereas SD patients showed increased zygomaticus responses to both positive and neutral videos. Controls showed greater arousal (SCL) when viewing positive and negative videos; however, both bvFTD and SD groups showed no change in SCL across conditions. Regardless of group membership, right insula damage was associated with dampened zygomaticus responses to positive film stimuli. Change in arousal (SCL) was associated with lower integrity of the caudate, amygdala, and temporal pole. Our results demonstrate that while bvFTD patients show an overall dampening of responses, SD patients appear to show incongruous facial emotional expressions. Abnormal responding is related to cortical and subcortical brain atrophy. These results identify potential mechanisms for the abnormal social behaviour in bvFTD and SD and demonstrate that psychophysiological responses are an important mechanism underpinning normal socioemotional functioning.

studies.abstract: The PET tracer [18F]florbetapir is a specific fibrillar amyloid-beta (Aβ) biomarker. During the late scan phase (> 40 min), it provides pathological information about Aβ status. Early scan phase (0-10 min) can provide FDG-'like' information. The current investigation tested the feasibility of using florbetapir as a dual-phase biomarker in behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD).

studies.title: Neuroanatomical correlates of apathy and disinhibition in behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia.
studies.abstract: Neuroanatomical correlates of apathy and disinhibition, behavioral abnormalities in behavioral variant Frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) remain unclear. In this study 45 participants (25 bvFTD patients and 20 controls) provided data on clinical, neuropsychological, behavioral (on Frontal Systems Behavior (FrSBe) Scale), cortical volume (on voxel-based morphometry (VBM)) and tract based spatial fractional anisotropy ((FA) on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), allowing examination of the neural correlates of apathy and disinhibition. The patients with bvFTD had predominant grey matter loss and corresponding white matter fractional anisotropy reduction in the frontal and temporal lobe compared to the controls. Grey matter loss in frontal, temporal and limbic structures correlated with apathy and degeneration in temporal limbic brain areas correlated with disinhibition. FA changes in inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus and forceps minor correlated with apathy and fibre integrity changes in the superior longitudinal fasciculus correlated with disinhibition. The current study suggests that apathy and disinhibition arises due to changes in the frontal, temporal and limbic brain areas  in bvFTD.

studies.title: Neural networks associated with body composition in frontotemporal dementia.
studies.abstract: Frontotemporal dementia (FTD) is associated with complex changes in eating behavior and metabolism, which potentially affect disease pathogenesis and survival. It is currently not known if body composition changes and changes in fat deposition also exist in FTD, the relationship of these changes in eating behavior and appetite, and whether these changes are centrally mediated.

studies.title: Variant-specific vulnerability in metabolic connectivity and resting-state networks in behavioural variant of frontotemporal dementia.
studies.abstract: Brain connectivity measures represent candidate biomarkers of neuronal dysfunction in neurodegenerative diseases. Previous findings suggest that the behavioural variant of frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) and its variants (i.e., frontal and temporo-limbic) may be related to the vulnerability of distinct functional connectivity networks. In this study, 82 bvFTD patients were included, and two patient groups were identified as frontal and temporo-limbic bvFTD variants. Two advanced multivariate analytical approaches were applied to FDG-PET data, i.e., sparse inverse covariance estimation (SICE) method and seed-based interregional correlation analysis (IRCA). These advanced methods allowed the assessment of (i) the whole-brain metabolic connectivity, without any a priori assumption, and (ii) the main brain resting-state networks of crucial relevance for cognitive and behavioural functions. In the whole bvFTD group, we found dysfunctional connectivity patterns in frontal and limbic regions and in all major brain resting-state networks as compared to healthy controls (HC N = 82). In the two bvFTD variants, SICE and IRCA analyses identified variant-specific reconfigurations of whole-brain connectivity and resting-state networks. Specifically, the frontal bvFTD variant was characterised by metabolic connectivity alterations in orbitofrontal regions and anterior resting-state networks, while the temporo-limbic bvFTD variant was characterised by connectivity alterations in the limbic and salience networks. These results highlight different neural vulnerabilities in the two bvFTD variants, as shown by the dysfunctional connectivity patterns, with relevance for the different neuropsychological profiles. This new evidence provides further insight in the variability of bvFTD and may contribute to a more accurate classification of these patients.

studies.title: Robust automated computational approach for classifying frontotemporal neurodegeneration: Multimodal/multicenter neuroimaging.
studies.abstract: Timely diagnosis of behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) remains challenging because it depends on clinical expertise and potentially ambiguous diagnostic guidelines. studies.title: Disease-specific profiles of apathy in Alzheimer's disease and behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia differ across the disease course.
studies.abstract: Apathy is one of the most prevalent and disabling non-cognitive symptoms of dementia. This loss of motivation and pervasive decline in goal-directed behaviour represents a core diagnostic feature of behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) and is also common in Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, despite growing recognition of a multidimensional model, apathy has typically been examined as a unitary symptom. Here, we employed a cross-sectional design to characterise the multidimensional nature of apathy across syndromes and disease course. 92 participants (44 bvFTD, 20 AD, 28 controls) completed the Dimensional Apathy Scale (DAS) to quantify emotional, executive, and initiation apathy. Patients were divided into early and late stages based on time since symptom onset. All participants underwent structural MRI and voxel-based morphometry was used to identify neural correlates of apathy dimensions. In the early stage of the disease (< 5 years since onset), emotional apathy was greater in bvFTD than AD. In contrast, in the late stage (> 5 years since onset), executive apathy was greater in AD than bvFTD, although apathy was elevated across all dimensions compared to controls. Notably, apathy was observed in the absence of self-reported depression in 46.2% of patients, with no patients classified as depressed only. Neuroimaging analyses revealed both common and divergent prefrontal and subcortical neural correlates associated with apathy dimensions. Our results reveal differing profiles of apathy across the disease course, in AD and bvFTD, with distinct brain regions mediating these dimensions. These findings will inform the development of appropriate treatment targets to ameliorate the impact of apathy in dementia.

studies.title: Scene construction impairments in frontotemporal dementia: Evidence for a primary hippocampal contribution.
studies.abstract: The capacity to generate naturalistic three-dimensional and spatially coherent representations of the world, i.e., scene construction, is posited to lie at the heart of a wide range of complex cognitive endeavours. Clinical populations with selective damage to key nodes of a putative scene construction network of the brain have provided important insights regarding the contribution of medial temporal and prefrontal regions in this regard. Here, we explored the capacity for atemporal scene construction, and its associated neural substrates, in the behavioural-variant of frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD); a neurodegenerative brain disorder in which atrophy systematically erodes medial and lateral prefrontal cortices with variable medial temporal lobe involvement. Nineteen bvFTD patients were compared to 18 typical Alzheimer's Disease (AD), and 25 healthy older Control participants on a scene construction task. Relative to Controls, both patient groups displayed marked impairments in generating contextually detailed and spatially coherent scenes, with bvFTD indistinguishable from AD patients across the majority of task metrics. Voxel-based morphometry, based on structural brain MRI, revealed divergent neural substrates of scene construction performance in each patient group. Despite widespread medial and lateral prefrontal atrophy, the capacity to generate richly detailed and spatially coherent scenes in bvFTD was found to rely predominantly upon the integrity of right medial temporal structures, including the hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus. Scene construction impairments in AD, by contrast, hinged upon the integrity of posterior parietal brain regions. Our findings in bvFTD resonate with a large body of work implicating the right hippocampus in the construction of spatially integrated scene imagery. How these impairments relate to changes in autobiographical memory and prospection in bvFTD will be an important question for future studies to address.

Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG‑PET was used), I5 (patient group size = 8 ≥ 6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (participants are described as FTD but the paper does not explicitly state they are clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD [bvFTD] or Pick’s disease), I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD group to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinates are reported). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (the paper does not present whole-brain voxelwise results; imaging is used for diagnostic/illustrative purposes rather than reporting voxelwise, coordinate-based group comparisons). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Given the absence of explicit bvFTD sampling and lack of whole-brain voxelwise between-group coordinates/results, the study cannot be included in the coordinate-based meta-analysis.

This VBM study includes a behavioral-variant FTD (FTD) subgroup (n=30) and reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM results, but it does NOT present a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD (FTD) to healthy controls in stereotactic space. Controls were explicitly not used in the VBM regressions, and the main findings are across a mixed patient sample (correlations with empathy) or subgroup-by-covariate interactions rather than a direct bvFTD vs. control group contrast with MNI/Talairach coordinates. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (no between-group contrast of bvFTD vs controls). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD/FTD patients included), I5 (adequate sample sizes for patient and control groups), I7 (reports whole-brain voxelwise results identified for the FTD subgroup via covariate interaction). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no direct between-group contrast of bvFTD vs controls reported). No exclusion criteria from the list were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: imaging modality is FDG-PET (I3); the sample comprises clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia patients per Lund–Manchester criteria with other FTLD variants (semantic dementia, non-fluent progressive aphasia) excluded, consistent with a behavioral-variant FTD sample (I4) — diagnosis based on clinical criteria and PET pattern; sample sizes meet minimums (29 patients, 16 controls) (I5); the paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing FTD to controls with coordinates reported in Talairach/MNI space (I6); whole-brain, voxelwise group-level SPM results are clearly identified as coming from the patient group (I7); results are reported as coordinates/figures and described in text (I8). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria were met.

This VBM study of frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) meets several inclusion criteria: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients with early prominent behavioural features consistent with bvFTD within the sample), I5 (≥6 patients and ≥6 controls), and I8 (reports whole-brain results in tables/figures). However it does NOT meet key meta-analysis requirements: I6 and I7 are not satisfied because the paper does not report a between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) group to healthy controls — instead analyses are performed on the mixed FTLD cohort (13 FTD + 3 SD) or on behavioural covariates within that pooled group. Therefore the target sample (bvFTD) is not isolated for a between-group voxelwise contrast, so the study cannot be included. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) .

Although this study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4), and has adequate group sizes (PGRN+ n=8, PGRN- n=8, controls) meeting the >=6 requirement (I5), it does NOT report a between-group whole-brain contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD-only group to controls (I6). The reported whole-brain VBM results are for genetic/pathological groups (PGRN+ and PGRN-) that include mixed clinical syndromes (bvFTD, SD, CBS), so the paper does not provide a group-level, whole-brain result clearly identified as coming solely from the target bvFTD sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet I6 and I7. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3, I4, I5. Inclusion IDs not met: I6, I7.

Full text is complete and the study is empirical, uses FDG-PET and includes clinically diagnosed frontal variant/bvFTD patients (n=13) and controls (n=21). It reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM results correlating autobiographical memory measures with resting FDG uptake in the fv-FTD group (i.e., group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results in stereotactic space). However, the paper does not present a between-group voxelwise contrast (bvFTD patients versus controls) reported in MNI/Talairach coordinates. Inclusion criterion I6 (at least one between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls in defined stereotactic space) is not met, so the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply.

Study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons in MNI space comparing clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD subjects to matched controls. Patient sample size (n=17 total; 7 with stereotypies, 10 without) and control group (matched, n≈17) both exceed the minimum of 6. The paper provides whole-brain group-level results (FTLD vs controls and direct FTLD subgroup comparisons) and details preprocessing in MNI space. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (systematic review, ROI-only, non-empirical, exclusively other modalities, or problematic comorbid samples) are met.

This study is excluded because it does not include a clinically defined behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease group as required by the review (inclusion criterion I4). Instead, participants are classified by pathological subtype (FTLD‐T and FTLD‐U) and while the majority “presented clinically as frontotemporal dementia,” the paper does not clearly define or isolate a bvFTD clinical group nor report between-group voxelwise contrasts specifically for a bvFTD group versus controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I5 (patient groups have ≥6 participants; controls n=61), I8 (whole-brain results presented in figures/tables). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (does not specify clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease group), I6 (no between-group contrast reported specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls in standardized stereotactic space), I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result identified as coming from a bvFTD target sample). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

While the study uses FDG-PET (meets I3), includes a patient group with Pick's disease / FTD and sufficient sample sizes (FTD n=14, controls n=33; meets I4 and I5), it does NOT report any group-level whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing bvFTD (or Pick's) to controls. The results are presented as diagnostic/visual assessments, region rating frequencies, and SSP individual-level statistical maps, but no whole-brain, group-level coordinate tables or voxelwise contrasts from the target patient group are provided. Therefore the study fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 and does not provide the necessary voxelwise whole-brain results. This places it within exclusion criterion E6 (no whole-brain results; only regional/visual/individual analyses).

This study reports FDG-PET (I3) on a clinically diagnosed frontal/behavioral variant FTD sample (bvFTD; I4). Imaging results are voxelwise SPM whole-brain analyses reported with Talairach coordinates and cluster statistics comparing patient groups to healthy controls (satisfies I6, I7, I8). PET subgroup sizes meet the minimum (H1 N=31, H2 N=10, controls N=16), and whole-brain between-group contrasts (H1 vs controls, H2 vs controls, and H1 vs H2) are reported, with coordinates provided. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the review.

This is an empirical VBM study that reports voxelwise group contrasts with coordinates comparing FTD patients to controls. Imaging modality: VBM (meets I3). Sample: includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients meeting Neary criteria and behavioral descriptions consistent with behavioral-variant FTD (meets I4). Sample sizes exceed thresholds (32 patients total, 27 with usable MRI; 47 controls) satisfying I5. The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts (overeating FTD subgroup vs nonovereaters and controls) with stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach reported), satisfying I6 and I8. VBM analyses are voxelwise/group-level whole-brain comparisons within an a priori ROI and results are clearly identified as coming from the target patient group (meets I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only without voxelwise results, not only FC/DTI/thickness, and no disqualifying comorbid sample issues). Note: the authors use the term “FTD” and Neary criteria rather than explicitly ‘bvFTD’; behavioral descriptions and diagnostic criteria indicate behavioral-variant FTD, which slightly reduces but does not preclude inclusion. Overall confidence 0.85.

This FDG-PET study includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients and meets imaging modality (I3), includes FTD (behavioral syndrome) patients (I4), and has sufficient patient numbers (I5). However, it does not report a between-group contrast comparing bvFTD (or FTD) to healthy controls: the main voxelwise comparisons are FTLD+UIC vs FTLD−UIC, and subgroup analyses restricted to FTD compare incontinent vs continent FTD patients (no healthy control group). Inclusion criteria I6 (bvFTD vs controls contrast) and I7 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise result originating from a bvFTD vs control contrast) are not met. The FTD-restricted results did not survive correction and are reported only uncorrected, and the primary analyses pooled FTLD subtypes. Therefore it does not satisfy the review’s requirement for bvFTD vs control whole-brain contrasts. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion IDs met: none.
Inclusion IDs met: I3 (study used voxelwise structural MRI analyses consistent with VBM-style processing).
Inclusion IDs NOT met: I4 (study does not specifically include clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD or explicitly Pick disease — cohort is mixed “FTD spectrum” and pathologically defined subgroups), I5 (for the voxelwise/group-level imaging contrasts relevant to this review, patient subgroup sizes are below the required minimum of 6: tau-positive n=5, tau-negative n=4, fv-AD n=3), I6 (no between-group contrast reported specifically comparing a clinically defined bvFTD group to controls without pooling), I7 (while whole-brain voxelwise results are reported, they are for pathologically defined subgroups, not for a clinically defined bvFTD group as required).
Therefore the study is excluded because it does not provide whole-brain voxelwise results for a clinically defined bvFTD/Pick group with sufficient sample size.
Full text completeness: full text appears complete.

This is a structural volumetric MRI study using lobar segmentation (Expectation-Maximization) rather than VBM, FDG-PET, or task/resting-state fMRI, so it does not meet the required imaging modality (I3 not met). The study does include clinically defined FTD patients meeting Neary criteria consistent with behavioral-variant FTD (I4 met) and has adequate sample sizes (FTD n=12, controls n=24) meeting I5. However, it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) and does not present whole-brain voxelwise group-level results for the bvFTD group (I6 and I7 not met). The analyses are regional/lobar volumetric (effectively ROI-based) with no whole-brain coordinate tables, so Exclusion E6 applies. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I6, I7. Exclusion criteria met: E6.

This is a longitudinal, empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (SPM2 optimized/modulated VBM) to compare MSTD (Tau +3 intron 10 mutation) patients to age- and gender-matched controls. The VBM analysis included 7 early-stage MSTD patients (all clinically diagnosed with bvFTD) and 19 controls, meeting the sample-size requirement. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts with significant clusters and refers to stereotactic locations in supplementary Table 4 (i.e., coordinates in a defined stereotactic space). Whole-brain voxelwise results are clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD-target sample. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, review/meta-analysis, methods-only, or disallowed imaging modalities) are met.

The study is excluded because it does not meet imaging and whole-brain reporting criteria required for the review. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (participants: clinically diagnosed FTD patients per Neary criteria, with semantic dementia and PNFA excluded, consistent with bvFTD sampling) and I5 (sample sizes: FTD n=44, controls present). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality) — the study used structural MRI lobar volumetry and automated regional volumes, not VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET; I6 (between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach) — no voxelwise coordinate-based group contrasts are reported; I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level result from target sample) — not provided. Exclusion criteria triggered: E6 (reports only ROI/lobar analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because it does not meet imaging-modality inclusion criterion I3: it uses SPECT (99mTc-ECD) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTD, i.e., bvFTD/fvFTD), I5 (patient group n=48; control group n=15), I6 (reports voxel coordinates in MNI space), I7 (reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM results), I8 (results reported with coordinates and described in text). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study included pathologically confirmed FTLD subjects including behavioural-variant FTLD subtypes (bvFTD) and used structural MRI with voxelwise grey-matter segmentation (VBM-style preprocessing) and had adequate sample size (n=19 FTLD). However, it does not report a between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrast directly comparing the bvFTD/FTLD group to healthy controls with coordinates in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The paper’s analyses focus on SVM classification (AD vs FTLD, AD vs controls, etc.) and visualization of voxels contributing to classifiers, but no explicit bvFTD-vs-control voxelwise group-level results or coordinate tables/thresholded statistical maps are provided for the target comparison. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7 required by the review.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD with adequate sample sizes (15 patients per bvFTD stage; 45 controls), reporting whole-brain voxelwise (SPM/VBM) group contrasts with MNI coordinates and corrected statistics. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. However, multiple participants across bvFTD groups had coexisting motor neuron disease (MND) (e.g., 5/15 in CDR 0.5, 5/15 in CDR 1, 3/15 in CDR 2–3), meaning the sample includes concurrent neurological disease. This violates exclusion criterion E7 (studies including participants with other neurological symptoms). The full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Because any single exclusion criterion mandates exclusion, the study is excluded.

This is an empirical multicenter FDG-PET study that includes a large FTD cohort (98 patients) explicitly described as the 'frontal variant' of FTD (i.e., behavioral variant). Imaging modality is FDG-PET (I3). Sample sizes exceed the minimum for patients and controls (I5). Scans were spatially normalized to the Talairach and Tournoux atlas and analyzed voxel-by-voxel with Neurostat/3D-SSP, producing group-level whole-brain voxelwise Z maps comparing FTD (frontal variant) to normals and other groups (I6, I7). Results are presented as whole-brain maps/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, no disqualifying comorbidities, and not a non-empirical methods-only paper). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study uses structural ROI-based MRI volumetrics rather than one of the required imaging modalities (I3 not met). Exclusion criterion E6 applies: the paper reports ROI/region-wise volumetric analyses and multivariate PLS relationships, but does not report whole-brain voxelwise (VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET) group-level contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) for a bvFTD group. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients, corresponding to bvFTD) and I5 (patient group n=8 and control groups >=6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (required imaging modality), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts in stereotactic space for bvFTD vs controls), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level result reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study uses voxelwise structural MRI analysis (RAVENS/voxel-based methods) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results, includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (including behavioral variant cases), and has adequate sample sizes (12 patients, 12 controls). However, the FTD group is pooled across subtypes (behavioral/executive, language variants, corticobasal), and the manuscript does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast specifically isolating a bvFTD (behavioral variant FTD) subgroup versus controls. Therefore it fails Inclusion Criterion I6 (bvFTD group not pooled with other patient groups in reported results). No exclusion criteria from the list are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons (FTLD/FTD vs controls) with coordinates in standardized space (MNI) and corrected results, fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements (I6,I7,I8). The sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD (behavioral variant/frontotemporal dementia) as a distinct subgroup (FTD n=15) within FTLD (I4), with adequate group sizes (FTLD n=25 total; VBM available in 21 FTLD and 17 controls) exceeding the minimum of 6 per group (I5). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, VBM analyses and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered: this is not a review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and it does not use excluded modalities. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study reports voxel-wise, whole-brain SPM analyses using FDG-PET and optimized VBM-MRI in a clinically diagnosed FTD sample (13 patients) with semantic dementia and progressive nonfluent aphasia specifically excluded (consistent with behavioral-variant FTD recruitment). Imaging modalities match (FDG-PET and VBM). Sample sizes meet the minimum (13 FTD, 20 controls). Data were normalized to MNI space and voxel-by-voxel group contrasts are reported (tables/figures) comparing FTD to controls and to AD — satisfying whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results in a defined stereotactic space. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria from the review appear to be violated. Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

Full text is complete. The study uses voxel-based morphometry (I3), includes clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD patients (behavioral FTD subgroup present; I4), has adequate sample sizes (62 patients, 14 controls; I5), and reports coordinates in Talairach space (I8). However, it does not report a between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD (behavioral FTD) subgroup to controls—the between-group comparison presented is for the entire mixed FTD group (violates I6). Also, the paper does not provide whole-brain group-level voxelwise results clearly identified as coming solely from the target bvFTD sample (violates I7). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTD group (FTD-fv, equivalent to bvFTD) (I4). Patient group sizes meet the minimum (25 FTD-fv patients; 22 CBS; controls n=14) (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts comparing the FTD-fv group to controls with results reported in MNI coordinates (e.g., crosshair 14,10,14) and FWE-corrected maps (I6, I7). Whole-brain results are presented in figures and described in text (I8). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided here, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical study of clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD (bvFTD) that uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts with MNI coordinates. Sample sizes meet thresholds (bvFTD N=26 overall; imaging subset bvFTD N=21, controls N=12; controls N=16 overall). The paper provides whole-brain VBM results (FTDp vs controls) with tables of MNI coordinates and SPM figures, and also reports ROI analyses; whole-brain results are clearly described. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, no excluded imaging modalities, and sample does not include confounding psychiatric or substance-abuse cases). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

Although the study is an empirical FDG-PET SPM study with adequate sample sizes and includes clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) patients (21/29), it does not present a between-group, voxelwise contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD-only group to healthy controls. The reported whole-brain results are for the broader FTLD group and subgroup contrasts based on anatomical/neuropsychological criteria, but bvFTD is not isolated as a target sample in a voxelwise bvFTD-versus-control analysis. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET imaging), I4 (bvFTD patients included), I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6), I8 (whole-brain results are reported in figures/tables). This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. The sample comprises clinically diagnosed frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) patients including a social/comportment & executive dysfunction subgroup (SOC/EXEC) consistent with behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) (I4). The study reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (31 patients) (I4) with an adequate sample size (31 bvFTD; 56 controls) meeting the ≥6 participant threshold (I5). It provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls and reports results on the Montreal Neurological Institute standard brain (MNI) with statistical parametric maps and coordinate-based tables/figures (I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not seed-FC/DTI/cortical-thickness only, and no evidence of disallowed comorbid sample). This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and includes 51 clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) patients (I4) and 14 healthy controls; group sizes exceed the minimum (I5). The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise VBM comparisons of the bvFTD group to controls and regional coordinates/BA results (tables/figure and supplemental Table e-1), satisfying between-group contrast reporting in standard space (I6) and providing whole-brain voxelwise results from the target sample (I7). This study meets all inclusion criteria for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and reports analyses restricted to the bvFTD subgroup (n=7 PGRN and n=11 MAPT) (I4); patient and control groups meet the minimum sample size (each patient subgroup ≥6; matched controls ≥6) (I5); reports group-level between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing disease groups (including the bvFTD-only analyses) to controls using SPM (voxelwise results in figures/tables/supplement) consistent with standard stereotactic space reporting (I6, I7); results are provided in figures and supplementary tables (I8). This autopsy-confirmed FTLD study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons. This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective. It used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as an imaging modality and explicitly reports VBM analyses (I3). Excluded because the study used manual region-of-interest volumetry (manual cortical parcellation) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and it reports ROI volumetric comparisons rather than whole-brain voxelwise results in stereotaxic coordinate space. Full text is complete and the study meets several inclusion criteria relevant to the review: it uses FDG‑PET imaging (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed frontal-variant frontotemporal dementia group (fv‑FTD, equivalent to bvFTD for diagnostic purposes) (I4), has sufficient sample sizes (fv‑FTD n=18; controls n=18) (I5), and reports whole‑brain, voxelwise group-level correlations/coordinates reported in Talairach space for the target patient groups (I7, I8). This is an empirical study that used FDG-PET and voxel-based morphometry (VBM), enrolled clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=24) and controls (n=12), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM/VBM results (MNI coordinates referenced, supplementary coordinates noted) comparing bvFTD subgroups to controls.
