Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD group directly to controls—analyses focus on correlations within patients and combined patient cohorts rather than bvFTD vs controls), I7 (no significant group-level whole-brain voxelwise result reported for the target group). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not meet the requirement for whole-brain, between-group voxelwise results and must be excluded.

This is an empirical study that reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients to healthy controls. The methods state VBM processing in SPM12 with normalization to MNI space and group-level voxelwise t-tests (cluster-based FWE correction) identifying regions of grey matter loss. Sample sizes meet thresholds (12 bvFTD patients, 20 controls). The paper provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results attributed to the bvFTD sample (figures and thresholded statistical images). Imaging modality (VBM), diagnostic group (bvFTD), adequate sample sizes, and voxelwise between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space are all satisfied. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (manual segmentation and shape analysis of caudate and putamen) using structural MRI, with no VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET voxelwise whole-brain analyses. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample) and I5 (sample sizes: 28 bvFTD, 26 controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is structural MRI/manual tracing, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrast results reported in MNI/Talairach stereotactic coordinates), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

The full text reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise analyses comparing diagnostic groups (including an autopsy-confirmed/amyloid-negative bvFTD group) to controls, with results reported at voxel level and coordinates referenced in supplementary tables. The study includes a large bvFTD sample (n=59) and controls (n=61), satisfying sample-size requirements. Imaging modality (VBM) meets I3; presence of clinically/neuropathologically defined bvFTD group meets I4; sample sizes meet I5; between-group voxelwise contrasts in stereotactic space with coordinates/tables meet I6 and I8; and the paper presents whole-brain group-level voxelwise results (I7). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, not limited to seed-based FC/DTI/thickness, and no disqualifying sample comorbidities reported for the bvFTD group). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports voxel-wise VBM analyses and a whole-brain two-sample t-test comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=20) to healthy controls (n=20), and also reports voxelwise regression results with MNI coordinates (e.g., IFG peak at −41,26,3). Imaging modalities include VBM (and FDG‑PET performed in most patients). Sample meets diagnostic criteria for bvFTD and exceeds the minimum sample sizes. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are reported and clearly attributed to the bvFTD group. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses VBM (voxel-based morphometry) alongside DTI (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=29) (I4), and has an adequate control group (n=37) and patient group sizes (>6) (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level VBM analyses and disease maps for the bvFTD group relative to controls using images in standard MNI space, with results summarized in figures/tables (I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply: it is an empirical study (not a review), includes whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only), and is not limited to only DTI/seed-based FC/cortical thickness methods. The provided full text is complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and supplementary references to figures/tables).

Full text is complete. Excluded because it reports manual ROI hypothalamic volume analyses only (no VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET and no whole-brain voxelwise/stereotactic coordinate results). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD group), I5 (bvFTD n=19 and controls n=23, both ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET—uses manual hypothalamic tracing on T1 MRI), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach coordinates), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). Therefore study is ineligible for the meta-analysis.

This study used structural MRI with VBM-based preprocessing (I3 satisfied) and included an FTD patient group (n≈12) and healthy controls (n=18) meeting minimum sample sizes (I5 satisfied). However, it does not specify behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease specifically (I4 not met). Critically, the paper reports SVM-based multivariate classification results rather than mass-univariate, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls; no group-level voxelwise results identified as coming from a bvFTD target sample are provided (I6 and I7 not met). Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria required for this review. No exclusion criteria from the list were triggered.

This empirical study uses voxel-based morphometry (FSL VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts (patient groups vs Controls) in MNI space. It includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=16) and healthy controls (n=17), both exceeding the minimum sample-size requirement. The manuscript reports voxel-wise atrophy analyses for bvFTD versus Controls, provides MNI coordinates and figures, and describes neural correlates of socio-emotional measures. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; no disallowed modalities; sample exclusions for psychiatric/substance comorbidity were applied appropriately). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and meets sample-size requirements (18 bvFTD, 20 controls) (I5). However, imaging methods are structural MRI cortical thickness ROI analyses using FreeSurfer rather than VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET, so it does not satisfy I3. The paper reports ROI-based cortical thickness correlations and ROI comparisons rather than any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in a standard space (MNI/Talairach), so it fails I6 and I7. Thus exclusion criteria E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and E9 (reports cortical thickness methods rather than allowed modalities) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

The full text is complete. Met inclusion criteria: I3 (uses VBM structural MRI), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD group, N=31), I5 (patient and control groups each ≥6; bvFTD N=31, controls N=75). Not met: I6 and I7 — the paper does not report any between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast comparing bvFTD vs healthy controls in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The primary VBM results are covariate-only regressions of BIS/BAS scores across the pooled sample and correlations that span diagnostic groups; co-atrophy checks control for diagnosis but no direct group-level bvFTD>control or bvFTD<control voxelwise contrast is presented. No exclusion criteria were triggered (e.g., it is not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it fails the requirement for a group-level whole-brain bvFTD vs control result and must be excluded.

This study uses VBM (I3 satisfied), includes clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD participants (bvFTD n=21; I4 satisfied), and meets the sample size requirement (≥6 bvFTD patients; I5 satisfied). However, the paper does not clearly report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrast in a defined stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach) that compares an isolated bvFTD group (not pooled with other patient groups) to healthy controls in the main text. While the authors state that VBM analyses of FTLD subgroups versus healthy controls are presented in the Supplementary material, the full text does not explicitly present a bvFTD versus control whole-brain coordinate-based contrast clearly attributable to the bvFTD group alone. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met from the provided full text. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study meets all imaging and sample criteria for inclusion. It reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses aligned to the MNI152 standard (explicitly stated), using voxelwise general linear models and permutation-based testing with familywise-error correction; results are presented as group-level whole-brain clusters (figures and supplementary tables referenced). The sample comprises clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD patients (58 meeting inclusion criteria) and a control group, both clearly reported and large enough (>6 participants). Between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls are described and localized in MNI space. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, empirical dataset, not solely seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used voxel-based morphometry (I3) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with sufficient sample sizes (22 patients, 22 controls) (I5). It reports between-group voxelwise contrasts aligned to MNI space (I6) and presents results in tables/figures (I8). However, the VBM analysis was performed within a predefined fronto-subcortical region-of-interest mask rather than as an unmasked whole-brain voxelwise analysis. Therefore the paper effectively reports ROI-restricted voxelwise results and does not provide the required group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) result from the target sample, violating the whole-brain evidence requirement (I7). Exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) is met. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I6, I8. Inclusion criterion not met: I7. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=24) and healthy controls (n=179), both exceeding the minimum sample size. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise VBM results including between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) with MNI coordinates, and additionally reports whole-brain interaction and region coordinates. Methods, results, and discussion are present and complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, not an unsupported imaging modality). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical FDG-PET study of clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (n=17) that reports voxel-wise, whole-brain SPM analyses (single-subject comparisons to a normative database and group-level one-sample t-tests) with results presented in SPM/MNI space. Imaging modality = FDG-PET; sample meets size requirement; group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from the bvFTD sample are described and overlaid on an MNI template. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review, ROI-only, non-empirical methods, disallowed modalities, or comorbid psychiatric/neurologic confounds) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria.

This study meets I3 (uses VBM, resting-state fMRI, and 18F-FDG PET), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; n=11), and I5 (bvFTD group size ≥6). However, it does not meet I6 or I7: there is no healthy/control group reported for between-group contrasts versus bvFTD, and the paper does not present group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (in MNI/Talairach space) comparing bvFTD to controls. Analyses are restricted to predefined ROI cores (voxelwise measures within those ROIs) and multivariate SVM classification; results are reported as classification accuracies rather than whole-brain coordinate-based between-group contrasts. Therefore the study reports only ROI-limited results with no qualifying whole-brain group contrasts and falls under exclusion E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a multi-center empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (normalized to MNI space) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts (FWE-corrected) comparing bvFTD to controls and to AD. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (final n=24) and controls (n=37), each >6 participants. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain VBM results (and TBSS DTI results) clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This empirical study meets the review objectives and all inclusion criteria. It uses resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (12 patients) with matched healthy controls (I4,I5), reports group-level between-group contrasts and analyses in standard stereotaxic/MNI space (SPM normalization and voxelwise VBM results) (I6), and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (thresholded and FDR-corrected) described in the text and supplementary materials (I7,I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete for screening purposes.

Exclusion criteria met: E6 and E9. This study reports ROI-based analyses (FreeSurfer cortical/WM ROIs and JHU DTI ROIs) and DTI/cortical-volume measures rather than voxelwise, whole-brain (voxelwise) results in standardized stereotactic space. It does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET as the primary imaging modality. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample, n=14) and I5 (patient group size >=6; AD comparison group n=19). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET as required), I6 (no between-group contrast reported in MNI/Talairach coordinate space), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore, exclude per E6 (only ROI analyses/no whole-brain results) and E9 (only DTI/cortical-volume methods rather than required modalities).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: I3 (uses voxel-based morphometry/voxel-wise gray matter analyses and ICA on T1-weighted MRI), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients diagnosed per Rascovsky criteria with multidisciplinary consensus and CSF measures), I5 (sample sizes exceed minimum: 24 bvFTD, 31 AD, 30 controls), I6 (reports between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls using voxelwise analyses in MNI space and SCN maps), I7 (provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results — TFCE, FWE-corrected VBM results and whole-brain SCN analyses), and I8 (results are presented and described in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, not solely seed-based FC/DTI/thickness). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore include for the review of bvFTD imaging studies.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group and reports whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons. Methods describe VBM preprocessing normalized to MNI space and whole-brain analyses; results include bvFTD vs. control voxelwise atrophy patterns and direct patient-group contrasts. Sample sizes meet the minimum (23 bvFTD patients; 50 controls). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, non-VBM modality, comorbid psychiatric/other-dementia sample, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is a genetic/clinical case series of TBK1 mutation carriers that includes several patients with behavioural-variant FTD and used FDG-PET in two patients (so I3, I4, and I5 are met: FDG-PET modality present; study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; there are ≥6 FTD patients in the cohort). However, the paper does not report any group-level between-group voxelwise contrasts in a standard stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls, nor any whole-brain, voxelwise group results or coordinate tables/figures suitable for meta-analysis. Therefore it fails I6 and I7. Because no whole-brain group results are provided, it falls under the exclusion of studies without whole-brain results (E6). Full text appears complete.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry and includes a clinical bvFTD sample (n=24) with healthy controls (n=24), and reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM findings for the bvFTD group. However, the VBM analyses described are within-group voxelwise correlations (neuroanatomical associations with language performance in the bvFTD group) rather than a between-group voxelwise contrast directly comparing bvFTD versus controls in stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) space. Inclusion criterion I6 (at least one between-group contrast comparing bvFTD group to controls) is not met. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore the paper must be excluded under the review rules.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) and healthy controls (n=12). The authors performed whole-brain, voxel-wise VBM analyses (TFCE, FWE-corrected) and report group-level between-group contrasts and anatomical coordinates in MNI space. Sample sizes meet the ≥6 requirement for patient and control groups. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (including imaging and VBM pipeline), Results (neuroimaging group contrasts and tables), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, no disqualifying comorbidities reported, and not limited to FC/DTI/cortical thickness). Therefore the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and should be included.

This empirical study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) normalized to MNI space and reports between-group (bvFTD vs. controls) voxelwise contrasts with cluster-level FWE correction (I3, I6, I7, I8). The sample comprises clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=26) and matched healthy controls (n=23), satisfying diagnostic and sample-size requirements (I4, I5). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (behavioral and MRI/VBM), Results (behavioral and VBM), and Discussion; core article content is present (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria are met: it is not a review/meta-analysis (E5), does not report only ROI analyses (E6), is empirical with original data (not E8), and does not rely solely on excluded imaging modalities (E9); participant selection excluded other neurological/psychiatric disorders (E7 not applicable). Therefore, INCLUDE.

The study is excluded because it reports only ROI/parcellation-based metabolic connectivity analyses (60 AAL VOIs) and does not present any whole-brain, voxelwise, coordinate-based (MNI/Talairach) between-group contrasts for behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) versus controls. The FTLD group is analyzed as a pooled group including behavioral and language variants, and bvFTD-specific results are not reported separately. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET imaging), I4 (includes behavioral-variant FTLD patients within the sample), I5 (sample sizes meet minimums). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group, coordinate-based voxelwise contrasts reported comparing bvFTD separately to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (study reports only ROI/parcellation-based analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical study that used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) and reports voxelwise results with MNI coordinates. It includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=19) and healthy controls (n=25), meeting sample-size thresholds. The paper describes whole-brain, group-level t-tests comparing patient groups (including bvFTD) to controls and reports VBM covariate analyses (MNI coordinates) linked to eating behavior and sucrose preference. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, no disqualifying comorbid sample, and not limited to seed‑based FC/DTI/cortical thickness). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text appears complete. Thus the study satisfies the required inclusion criteria for the review.

The study used VBM and resting-state fMRI (I3) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (7 bvFTD cases within the FTD-GRN+ group) (I4). Sample sizes meet minimums (14 patients, control groups ≥6) (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group results (VBM and functional maps) (I7) and presents results in figures/tables (I8). However, the critical requirement I6 is not met: the reported between-group contrasts compare a combined FTD-GRN+ group (mixing bvFTD and avPPA) to controls rather than reporting a bvFTD-only versus control whole-brain contrast. The bvFTD subgroup is pooled with other FTD phenotypes in the main analyses, so no bvFTD-specific whole-brain contrast is available. No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for failing inclusion criterion I6.

This is an original empirical neuroimaging study of clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (Rascovsky criteria). It used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on MRI and FDG-PET with voxelwise SPM5 analyses and partial-volume correction, reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (patients vs. controls) with tables/figures in stereotactic space. Sample size is 15 bvFTD patients and 15 matched healthy controls (>=6 each). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria were met (not a review, not ROI-only, no comorbid psychiatric/substance cases, not non-empirical, and not only seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness). Therefore the paper meets all required inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical resting-state fMRI study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD (I3, I4) with adequate sample sizes (14 bvFTD, 12 controls) meeting I5. However, the paper performs ROI-based graph-theory analyses (AAL parcellation, Network Centrality averaged across ROIs) and reports network-level differences rather than voxelwise, whole-brain coordinate results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). Therefore it does not meet I6 and I7 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach) and qualifies for exclusion under E6 (reports only ROI/network analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. Exclusion criteria applied: E6.

This study used VBM (I3), included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=13, I4), and had adequate sample sizes for patients and controls (bvFTD n=13; controls n=20, I5). However, the VBM analyses reported are correlational within a combined patient cohort and significant effects were reported only within pre-specified regions of interest; no between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD versus controls in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) are presented, and no whole-brain group-level voxelwise results for the bvFTD group are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. This meets exclusion criterion E6 (reports only ROI findings / no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=33) with healthy controls (n=34). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise two-sample t-tests were performed in MNI space with results reported (figures and supplementary tables of coordinates) for bvFTD versus controls; cerebellar analyses used SUIT but whole-brain VBM results for the cerebral cortex are presented. The bvFTD group was not pooled with other patient groups in the reported between-group contrasts. Sample sizes exceed the minimum. Therefore all required inclusion criteria for VBM studies of bvFTD are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clearly defined bvFTD patient group (n=22) and age-matched controls (n=38). The paper uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and reports voxelwise, whole-brain (voxelwise GLM with permutation testing) group contrasts between bvFTD and controls with MNI coordinates and cluster thresholds provided (I6, I7). Sample sizes meet the minimum (I5). The bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled) and the paper provides group-level whole-brain results in the main text and supplementary tables/figures (I4, I8). Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables/figures descriptions, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and should be INCLUDED.

This empirical study reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses of both 18F-FDG PET and voxel-based morphometry (GM density) comparing a bvFTD patient group to healthy controls. It used SPM8 with customized templates, reports Talairach-corrected coordinates and cluster-level inference, and presents group-level between-group contrasts for the whole bvFTD sample and bvFTD subgroups (bvFTD+ and bvFTD−) vs controls. Sample sizes meet thresholds (25 patients, 20 controls). The bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, no disallowed imaging-only methods, and no comorbid psychiatric/other dementia confounds). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

The study reports VBM and DTI analyses in clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and controls with MNI coordinates provided (I3, I4, I5, I6 satisfied). However, the imaging analyses were conducted using an ROI mask confined to predefined motor-system regions rather than reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results. Therefore it does not provide whole-brain voxelwise results from the target sample (I7 not met) and meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the key disease-sample and contrast requirements for inclusion. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (voxel-based morphometry was used) and I5 (patient groups, e.g., FTLD n=55, exceed the minimum of 6 participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the sample does not report a clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease group specifically — participants are classified by pathological FTLD subtypes rather than a bvFTD clinical subgroup), I6 (no between-group contrast is reported specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space — reported contrasts are for FTLD/FTLD subgroups, not bvFTD), and I7 (there is no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target sample). Exclusion criteria met: none (no applicable exclusion criteria such as review-only, ROI-only, DTI/FC-only, comorbid sample, or non-empirical). Full text appears complete. Because the review requires results specifically for clinically defined bvFTD (or Pick’s) groups and voxelwise between-group contrasts for that group, this paper cannot be included.

Full text reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses: images normalized to MNI space and whole-brain voxel-wise comparisons were performed. Sample includes 18 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (per diagnostic criteria) and 18 healthy controls (both >6). The paper reports between-group whole-brain contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) and regression analyses relating atrophy to behavior, with results presented in figures/tables. This meets imaging modality (I3), bvFTD sample (I4), sample size (I5), between-group MNI-space contrasts (I6), whole-brain group-level voxelwise results (I7), and acceptable reporting formats (I8). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; no prohibited modalities; no disqualifying comorbidities reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study used atlas-based ROI volumetry on T1-weighted MRI (no VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) and reports only region-of-interest volumetric comparisons without any whole-brain voxelwise (MNI/Talairach) coordinates or group-level voxelwise contrasts comparing a bvFTD group to controls. Exclusion criterion met: E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants) and I5 (patient groups and control group sizes meet the ≥6 threshold). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrast reported in a defined stochastic space for bvFTD vs controls), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results). Full text appears complete.

Exclusion applied: E9 (study reports only cortical thickness methods). Inclusion met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample included), I5 (sufficient sample sizes: 37 bvFTD, 33 controls), I7 (whole-brain vertex-wise cortical thickness analyses performed), I8 (results reported with supplementary material). Inclusion not met: I3 (required imaging modality VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET — this study used structural MRI cortical thickness and subcortical volumetry via FreeSurfer), I6 (unclear/no between-group results reported in a defined stereotactic coordinate space such as MNI/Talairach; vertex-wise surface results do not provide standard voxel coordinates in the paper text). The full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded because it uses cortical thickness methods (excluded by E9) and does not meet the required imaging modalities (I3).

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=84) and uses whole-brain VBM (I3, I4, I5 satisfied) and reports voxelwise results/coordinates (I8 satisfied), it does not report any between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls (no control group or bvFTD-vs-control voxelwise contrast). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 (bvFTD vs controls contrast) and I7 (whole-brain voxelwise result originating from the bvFTD vs control comparison). Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clearly defined bvFTD subgroup (n=64) and compares clinical phenotypes (including bvFTD) to healthy controls (n=32) using whole-brain voxelwise analyses. Imaging modality is VBM (I3). The sample contains clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and the bvFTD group and controls exceed the 6-participant minimum (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results for each phenotype vs controls and specifies statistical thresholds and cluster reporting; results for bvFTD vs controls are described and illustrated (I6, I7). The manuscript references figures and supplementary material for spatial results (acceptable per I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Although coordinate tables are not embedded in the provided excerpt, the methods and references to figures/supplementary materials indicate voxelwise results in a standard space; thus the study meets inclusion criteria for this review.

This is a VBM study that includes bvFTD patients (7/10 in the SQSTM1 carrier group), uses whole-brain VBM, and has adequate group sizes; however, the reported whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are for the mixed FTD/SQSTM1 carrier group (which includes bvFTD and other FTD subtypes) rather than a bvFTD-only group. The review requires at least one between-group whole-brain contrast clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD group that is not pooled with other patient groups (I6, I7). Because the study does not report bvFTD-specific whole-brain contrasts, it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 and must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it reports only ROI-based structural MRI and ASL perfusion analyses rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET voxelwise whole-brain analyses. Exclusion ID met: E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients) and I5 (patient group N=11 and control group N=20, both ≥6). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (does not report between-group contrasts in standard coordinate space [MNI/Talairach] for voxelwise results), and I7 (does not report group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Given these mismatches with the imaging and whole-brain reporting criteria, the study does not meet all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=15) (I4) and healthy controls (n=20) with adequate sample sizes (>6) (I5). The paper reports between-group VBM contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls and provides whole-brain voxelwise results in MNI space, including tables/figures of atrophy patterns and coordinates (I6, I7, I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria are met (no review/meta-analysis only, not ROI-only, not seed-based FC/DTI/cortical-thickness only, and sample comorbidities are exclusionary criteria but are not present).

The study is excluded because it does not use the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) required by I3, and it does not report between-group coordinates in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) required by I6. It does include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=9) and controls (n=18) satisfying I4 and I5, and it reports whole-brain voxelwise DTI (TBSS) results (I7). However, the meta-analysis requires specific modalities (I3), which are absent (study uses DTI, ASL perfusion, and structural ROI volumetry), and no between-group coordinate-based contrasts for bvFTD vs controls are provided (I6 not met). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses to examine neural correlates of empathy in clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients. The sample includes 24 bvFTD patients and 22 healthy controls (both >6). The paper reports voxel-wise, whole-brain between-group contrasts and covariate analyses with anatomical results reported in MNI stereotaxic space (coordinates and tables/figures referenced). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only analysis, excluded comorbid samples, non-empirical methods) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis focused on bvFTD VBM studies.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (23 patients included) with a healthy control group (20 controls). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise VBM group comparisons (two-sample t-test) showing atrophic clusters in bilateral anterior temporal lobes and additional regions, and voxelwise regression analyses relating behavioral measures to GM volume in the patient group. Imaging modality includes VBM (and FDG-PET performed in most patients). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (patients=23, controls=20). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results comparing bvFTD to controls are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods (including VBM preprocessing and statistics), Results (behavior and imaging) and Discussion; core article content is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and the reporting allowance I8. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

The full text reports voxelwise whole-brain structural MRI analyses (gray matter probability images processed with ANTs and Randomise permutation-based voxelwise tests in MNI space), meeting the imaging-modality requirement (I3). The sample includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=54) and healthy controls (n=27), meeting I4 and I5. The paper reports between-group GM atrophy contrasts and whole-brain regression analyses comparing each patient group (including bvFTD) to controls in stereotactic space (MNI), satisfying I6 and I7; whole-brain results are described in text/tables/figures (I8). The full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical study with FDG-PET and MRI in a clinically characterized bvFTD cohort, but it does not report any voxelwise/whole-brain (MNI/Talairach) between-group coordinate results. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (patient group N=27 ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain/voxelwise results), I8 (no whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures in standard space). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were directly triggered. Therefore exclude because key whole-brain/voxelwise reporting requirements (I6–I8) are not satisfied.

This study meets the review objective and all relevant imaging and sample criteria: (I3) uses Voxel-Based Morphometry (SPM8 VBM) as the imaging modality; (I4) includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=104, with 90 included in VBM analyses); (I5) adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n≈90; controls n=44); (I6) reports between-group VBM contrasts comparing bvFTD subgroups and the bvFTD cohort to age-matched controls (voxelwise T-maps reported and described); (I7) provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (FWE-corrected whole-brain VBM maps); (I8) whole-brain results are presented in figures and described in text (supplementary material referenced). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplemental materials are acknowledged. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Therefore the paper is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of whole-brain imaging in bvFTD.

The full text reports resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) and diffusion MRI analyses; rs-fMRI (ICA/dual-regression of the DMN) satisfies imaging modality criterion (I3). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12) and controls (n=17), meeting I4 and I5 (both groups ≥6). The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (Randomise, one-way ANCOVA and post-hoc t-tests) for DMN connectivity and TBSS-based DTI metrics; results are reported as cluster-based whole-brain findings with reference to supplement tables (acceptable per I6 and I8). Whole-brain voxelwise evidence from the target bvFTD group is clearly presented (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: this is an empirical study (not a review), reports whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only), and does not ONLY report seed-based FC, DTI, or cortical thickness (it includes whole-brain rs-fMRI ICA results). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This study reports VBM analyses and provides MNI coordinates relating gray matter atrophy to behavioral measures in bvFTD and AD, and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=39) and controls (n=61). However, the VBM analyses were constrained to an a priori ROI mask (Papez circuit and prefrontal regions) rather than reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results. The paper therefore appears to present ROI-limited voxelwise results only and does not provide an unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise contrast for the bvFTD group vs. controls. According to the review criteria, whole-brain evidence is required; because only ROI-restricted analyses are reported, this meets exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I6. Inclusion criterion not met: I7. Exclusion criterion met: E6.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses FDG-PET imaging (I3); includes clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (Rascovsky criteria) (I4) with N=52 (I5); reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses including a two-sample t-test comparing the bvFTD group (and subgroups) to a normal image database (n=112), i.e., between-group contrasts in stereotactic space (I6, I7). Whole-brain voxelwise results are described (and likely presented as SPM maps/figures), satisfying the acceptable reporting formats (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not a review, not ROI-only, not seed-based FC/DTI/cortical-thickness-only, and sample exclusions do not apply). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports empirical imaging and behavioral data on clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=14) and age-matched controls (n=19). It includes voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses and resting-state fMRI connectivity, reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts and coordinates (e.g., ATL [-45,13,-37]; IFG [-52,2,14]) in standard space, and provides group-level results comparing bvFTD to controls. Sample sizes meet thresholds. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (reviews, ROI-only, comorbid psychiatric/other dementia confounds, non-empirical, or limited-to-seed-only methods) apply based on provided content.

This study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants and reports voxelwise longitudinal structural MRI analyses, but it analyzes bvFTD and svPPA combined as a single FTLD group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (voxelwise structural MRI/voxel-based morphometry–type analysis of gray-matter change), I4 (bvFTD patients included in sample), I5 (patient and control group sizes >6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast reported that isolates bvFTD vs controls; bvFTD data are pooled with svPPA), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results are reported for the combined FTLD group, not clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target group). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This empirical study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons of bvFTD patients (two bvFTD subgroups) versus healthy controls. Participants meet clinical bvFTD criteria (revised criteria) and group sizes are sufficient (34 bvFTD patients; 30 controls). The manuscript describes whole-brain VBM contrasts (AbvFTD vs controls; DbvFTD vs controls; AbvFTD vs DbvFTD) with FDR-corrected results and refers to Supplementary Table/Figure for VBM findings (coordinate tables/figures reported). Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete and the study does include VBM (I3), clinically diagnosed bv-FTD participants (n=15) (I4), and adequate group sizes with controls (I5). However, it does NOT report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast that isolates the bvFTD group versus controls in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The VBM results presented compare a subgroup defined by poor melody scores to controls and report correlations across pooled patient groups; they do not provide a bvFTD-specific voxelwise contrast or coordinates. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because the paper lacks bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain voxelwise results in stereotactic space (I6 and I7 not satisfied).

This is an empirical, longitudinal resting-state fMRI study (also includes VBM) comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12) to controls (n=22). The paper reports voxel-wise, whole-brain group-level contrasts and longitudinal voxel-based analyses (permutation testing, FWE correction) with results presented in figures/tables, comparing bvFTD versus controls (bvFTD not pooled). Whole-brain network-to-region and VBM results are described, satisfying requirements for stereotactic reporting and acceptable presentation formats. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, irrelevant modalities, or disallowed comorbid samples) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The full text reports voxel-based morphometry and resting-state fMRI analyses (I3). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=26) (I4) and a healthy control group (n=22), meeting the minimum sample size requirement (I5). The paper presents whole-brain, voxelwise between-group VBM contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls with coordinate tables referenced in the Supplementary material (I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply: this is an empirical study with whole-brain VBM and fMRI results, without pooling bvFTD with other patient groups for the reported contrasts. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical study that used FDG-PET (and ASL-MRI) and included a clearly clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=32) with cognitively normal controls (n=15). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons (GLM and PLS logistic regression) with images normalized to a template and presents group-level voxelwise results contrasting bvFTD vs. controls and bvFTD vs. AD (figures and voxelwise analyses). The sample sizes exceed the minimum, and results are presented as whole-brain voxelwise maps (figures and statistical parametric maps) suitable for inclusion. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the record appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (36 bvFTD plus 20 FTD-ALS) (I4); has adequate sample sizes (56 patients, 23 healthy controls) (I5); reports voxel-wise between-group contrasts and VBM analyses performed in MNI space with coordinates provided (including supplementary material) (I6); presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for the target sample (I7); and allows coordinates/results in supplements/figures as acceptable (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is an empirical VBM whole-brain study (not a review, ROI-only, DTI/FC-only, or non-empirical), and the sample exclusions (e.g., substance abuse, TBI) were applied by the authors. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical resting-state fMRI study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=21) and healthy controls (n=25), uses voxel-based morphometry and whole-brain ICA/dual-regression voxelwise analyses in MNI space, and reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls (including MNI coordinates). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study uses whole-brain VBM and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=58) with controls (n=44), but its reported voxelwise analyses are brain–behavior correlations across a pooled neurodegenerative sample rather than between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls. The paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) result clearly identified as coming solely from the bvFTD group (no bvFTD vs control contrast in MNI/Talairach space reported). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 despite meeting I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: (I3) it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for structural MRI analyses; (I4) includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (16 probable bvFTD patients diagnosed by expert consensus); (I5) sample sizes meet thresholds (16 bvFTD patients and 22 healthy controls); (I6) reports between-group VBM contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls (whole-brain two-sample comparisons with explicit statistical thresholds and MNI normalization described); (I7) presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for the target bvFTD group (FWE-corrected results reported, and comparisons bvFTD>controls and bvFTD>BD described); (I8) results/coordinates are indicated as reported in figures/tables (methods state normalization to MNI space and VBM outputs). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion; core article content is present (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply. Overall, the paper provides whole-brain VBM evidence for bvFTD vs controls and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This empirical study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria: it uses FDG-PET with voxel-wise (SPM) analyses (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=26) (I4) and a healthy control group (n=24) with both groups >6 participants (I5). The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts in standard space comparing bvFTD to controls and subgroup contrasts (amnestic vs non-amnestic bvFTD) (I6). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are presented and described in the text and figures/tables (I7, I8). No exclusion criteria are met: it is not a review/meta-analysis (E5), does not report only ROIs (E6), excludes comorbid psychiatric/neurological confounds per methods (E7), is empirical with original data (E8), and does not rely solely on seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness methods (E9). The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study examines presymptomatic C9ORF72 expansion carriers (preSxC9), not clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick's disease patients; therefore it does not meet the core population requirement. Although the paper provides whole-brain VBM and resting-state fMRI voxelwise contrasts comparing preSxC9 to controls, these contrasts are not derived from a bvFTD patient group (so I6 and I7 are not satisfied). It does satisfy I3 (uses VBM and resting-state fMRI), I5 (patient group N=15 and control groups >6), and I8 (reports whole-brain voxelwise results in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on structural MRI (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (52 patients, diagnosed per current criteria) (I4); has adequate sample sizes (52 patients, 52 controls) (I5); reports between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls in MNI space (I6); presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (voxelwise GLM, FWE-corrected) clearly identified as from the target bvFTD sample (I7); and reports results in figures/tables/coordinates as described (I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion provided (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Full text is complete. The study meets I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; n=16), and I5 (bvFTD group n>=6; healthy controls n=19). However it does NOT report any voxelwise between-group contrast (bvFTD vs. controls) in stereotactic space attributable specifically to the bvFTD group; VBM results are reported as brain–behavior correlations across the whole combined sample and co-atrophy-adjusted analyses, not as group-level whole-brain contrasts for bvFTD alone. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I6/I7 are not, the study must be excluded.

This study includes FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD patients (I4) with adequate sample sizes (20 FTD patients; controls n=38) satisfying I5. However, the paper reports visual assessment of individual Z-maps and reader-based diagnostic performance rather than reporting any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space (no coordinates or voxelwise statistical maps for bvFTD vs controls are provided). Therefore it does not meet I6 and I7 (no group-level voxelwise contrast or whole-brain results for the target sample). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria were triggered.

This is an empirical, whole-brain, voxel-wise longitudinal MRI study of frontotemporal lobar degeneration that includes a distinct bvFTD group (n=44) and controls (n=97). The methods use voxel-wise gray-matter contraction/expansion maps computed with SPM12 and DARTEL, normalized to MNI space, and report between-group t-maps and consensus voxelwise ROIs comparing bvFTD to controls. Sample sizes exceed the minimum. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for bvFTD versus controls are presented (figures, maps, and effect sizes). No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, seed-based FC/DTI/cortical-thickness-only) apply. Full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This study is excluded because it does not include clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease participants. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study used Voxel-Based Morphometry) and I5 (patient groups and control group sizes exceed 6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (participants are not clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease — groups are pathology-confirmed diagnoses including FTLD-tau and TDP43 subtypes but clinical syndromes like bvFTD are not specified), I6 (no between-group contrast reported specifically comparing a clinically-defined bvFTD group to controls), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target sample). No exclusion criteria from the list were triggered. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical multicenter study using resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) that enrolled 52 clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients and 60 matched healthy controls. It reports group-level, whole-brain VBM results normalized to MNI space and between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls (and to other patient groups), with voxelwise/statistical maps and supporting tables. Sample sizes exceed the 6-participant minimum. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, excludes comorbid psychiatric diagnoses). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

Although the study uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (meets I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=14, meets I4) and has >=6 patients and >=6 controls (meets I5), it does NOT report any between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD group directly to controls in MNI/Talairach space. Imaging analyses are reported as correlations between PCA-derived component scores and grey/white matter across a mixed diagnostic cohort rather than a group-level bvFTD vs control VBM contrast. Therefore criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses VBM (FSL-VBM) for whole-brain grey matter analyses (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=7) (I4) with ≥6 patients and healthy controls (n=40) (I5); reports between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI space and provides MNI coordinates/figures for phenotype-specific whole-brain results including bvFTD versus controls (I6,I7); qualifying whole-brain results are presented in figures and text (I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, and no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the review focused on bvFTD VBM whole-brain studies.

The full text reports an empirical study including a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=27) and healthy controls (n=48). It uses resting-state fMRI (RS fMRI) as an imaging modality (plus TBSS/DTI and cortical thickness). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (TBSS and dual-regression RS-fMRI) with results displayed on the MNI standard brain and describes between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls and bvFTD vs EOAD) in standard space. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). The report contains complete Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, no disallowed participant comorbidities, and not limited to seed-based FC/DTI/cortical-thickness-only). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical VBM study that directly investigates bvFTD. It uses voxel-based morphometry (FSL VBM) (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=25) (I4) and healthy controls (n=25) with adequate sample sizes (>6) (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) with results provided in stereotaxic space (MNI) and discusses voxelwise group-level findings (I6, I7, I8). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria were violated: this is not a review/meta-analysis (not E5), whole-brain results are reported (not E6), participants with psychiatric/other dementia/substance-abuse were explicitly excluded from recruitment (so E7 not met), it is empirical (not E8), and it does not report only seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness (not E9). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

Excluded because the imaging modality is surface-based cortical thickness analysis of structural MRI rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET — this fails inclusion criterion I3 and meets exclusion criterion E9 (cortical thickness-only study). The study does meet I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample) and I5 (sample sizes: 88 bvFTD, 30 controls). It also provides whole-brain vertex-wise analyses (satisfying I7) and reports results in figures/supplementary materials (I8). However, it does not report between-group results in stereotaxic coordinates (MNI/Talairach), so I6 is not met. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study uses voxel-wise gray matter density analysis on high-resolution T1 MRI with Randomise in FSL and reports whole-brain group comparisons and regressions relating f0 range to GM atrophy. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=32) and matched healthy controls (n=17), exceeding the minimum sample size. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts and regression results (with family-wise error correction, TFCE) and references peak voxels summarized in table e-1 (supplement), satisfying requirements for reporting coordinates/whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; no disallowed modalities). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided; supplemental tables are referenced but their absence does not render the core full text incomplete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This empirical study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on 3T MRI and reports voxelwise group analyses. The sample includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=19) and healthy controls (n=20), meeting minimum sample-size requirements. The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing patient groups (bvFTD and SD) to controls (voxel-wise two-sample t-tests) with results referenced to MNI space and statistical parametric maps/tables presented. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for the bvFTD group versus controls are reported (atrophy maps and VBM behavioural correlates). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not DTI/FC-only, and patient sample appears free of excluded comorbidities). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for bvFTD neuroimaging VBM studies.

Study meets several inclusion criteria: it used FDG-PET (I3), included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=90) (I4), and has sufficient sample sizes (I5). However, the full text does not provide a clear between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast reported in a defined stereotactic space (MNI or Talairach) for the bvFTD group versus controls. Although preprocessing used MNI normalization and voxelwise SPM analyses were performed for the overall FTLD group, the manuscript does not present coordinates or an explicit group-level voxelwise contrast for bvFTD (I6 and I7 not satisfied). Therefore it cannot be included for coordinate-based meta-analysis.

Exclusion E6 met: the study uses ROI-based graph/network analyses of resting-state fMRI (220 predefined regions and network-based statistics) and does not report voxelwise whole-brain group-level coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (resting-state fMRI used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients included; n=38), I5 (patient and control groups each >=6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast reported in defined stereotactic space with coordinates), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level result clearly reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded because it fails the requirement for voxelwise/coordinate-based whole-brain results and falls under E6.

This study reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) results relating regional atrophy to behavioural ratings within a bvFTD patient group and includes appropriate sample sizes and controls; however it does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast (bvFTD vs. healthy controls) in MNI/Talairach space. Specifically: Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (≥6 patients and controls: 25 bvFTD, 21 controls), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise VBM results derived from the target bvFTD sample), I8 (results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 — the paper does not present at least one between-group whole-brain contrast comparing bvFTD to controls (patient-only regressions/correlations reported instead). Because I6 is required, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with autopsy-confirmed diagnoses and voxel-wise whole-brain analyses. The paper reports voxel-based morphometry (W-score) maps, frequency maps, and linear discriminant voxelwise maps comparing bvFTD patients to controls and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results in figures (Figs 3–4) and supplementary material. Sample size for patients with imaging (n=82) exceeds the minimum (≥6). The methods explicitly describe voxel-wise, whole-brain analyses in standard space and comparisons to control data to generate W-scores. Although coordinate tables are not shown in the extracted text, whole-brain voxelwise group results are clearly reported in figures and described in the text, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level results for the bvFTD group. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM study of bvFTD that reports whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts and correlations in standard coordinate space. The paper uses voxel‑based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=20 total; N=17 in MRI subset) and healthy controls (N=39 total; N=28 MRI subset), and both patient and control groups exceed the 6‑participant threshold. The authors report VBM atrophy contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls and report voxelwise clusters with coordinates (MNI/Talairach) for both masked reward‑network and whole‑brain analyses. Whole‑brain voxelwise results are clearly described in the text and include coordinate data. Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study uses structural volumetric MRI with FreeSurfer ROI analyses, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and it does not report whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts comparing bvFTD to healthy controls. Inclusion met: I4 (bvFTD patients included; bvFTD n=26) and I5 (patient group size ≥6). This resting-state fMRI study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=50) and controls (n=32) and uses seed-based, network-based (NBS), and graph-theory analyses; however, it does not report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in a standard coordinate space (MNI/Talairach) for the bvFTD vs control contrast. Analyses are AAL-atlas node/ROI-based (NBS and graph metrics) and seed-based FC results are reported as disconnected regions/nodes rather than voxelwise coordinates. Therefore it fails the meta-analysis requirements for coordinate-based, whole-brain between-group contrasts. Exclusion applied per E6 (ROI-only/no whole-brain results) and E9 (reports only seed-based/ROI-based FC methods without coordinate-based voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (resting-state fMRI), I4 (bvFTD sample), I5 (sample sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 and I7 (no clearly reported between-group contrast in defined coordinate space; no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This is a single-case clinical genetic case report of childhood-onset cerebellar ataxia due to a homozygous SQSTM1 mutation, not a study of behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). It does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (violates I3); the sample does not include clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease patients (violates I4); patient group size is N=1, below the required minimum of 6 (violates I5); no between-group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls are reported (violates I6); and no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results from a target bvFTD sample are presented (violates I7/I8). No exclusion criteria from the list are specifically met. Therefore the study does not satisfy the required inclusion criteria for this review and is excluded.

This article is a narrative review (non-empirical) of neuroimaging findings in DLB, FTLD, and iNPH rather than an original empirical study. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (systematic review/meta-analysis or review article) and E8 (non-empirical paper without original data). Inclusion criteria met: none []. Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (the paper itself does not present original VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET data from the authors as an empirical study), I4 (no original sample of clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick disease reported), I5 (no patient or control group sample sizes reported as original data; therefore no ≥6 participants), I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space from an original bvFTD sample), I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise results from the target sample), I8 (not applicable — no original whole-brain coordinate tables/figures from a primary bvFTD sample). Full text completeness: fulltext_incomplete=false (full review text present).

This study should be excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) volumetric analyses (frontal-lobe regional volumes derived from multi-atlas segmentation of T1 MRI) rather than VBM, task/resting‑state fMRI, or FDG‑PET voxelwise results. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain/voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; n=18) and I5 (bvFTD group size ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is volumetric T1 segmentation, not VBM/fMRI/FDG‑PET), I6 (no between-group contrast reported in stereotactic coordinates comparing bvFTD to controls), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain/voxelwise results). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper does not provide the required whole-brain voxelwise coordinate-based results and must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not provide bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise results with an adequate bvFTD sample. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses resting-state fMRI) and I4 (included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (bvFTD subgroup N=4, which is <6 required), I6 (no reported between-group contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD-only group to controls—the paper reports an aggregated FTD group and discusses FTD subtypes pooled), and I7 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target sample alone). No exclusion criteria from the provided list apply. The full text appears complete. Because the meta-analysis objective specifically targets bvFTD and requires bvFTD-specific, whole-brain contrasts with sufficient sample size, this study must be excluded.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FSL VBM), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (44 bvFTD patients; 36 with usable MRI scans), includes sufficient sample sizes (bvFTD n>=6; controls n>=6), and reports between-group whole-brain contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls with results presented in MNI space (voxelwise GLMs, permutation testing, cluster/coordinate reporting). The full text contains introduction, methods, results (including neuroimaging findings and MNI coordinates/figures/tables), and discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore include for meta-analysis.

The article reports whole-brain VBM analyses (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=19) alongside healthy controls (n=25), meeting sample size requirements (I4, I5). The study reports between-group voxelwise contrasts and correlations in MNI space (I6) and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results attributable to the bvFTD group (I7). Results are described in the text and supplementary material (I8). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is empirical (not a review), includes whole-brain VBM (not ROI-only), excludes participants with other neurological/psychiatric conditions per methods, and does not rely solely on methods excluded (e.g., seed-based FC, DTI, cortical thickness). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is a single-case report (n=1) and does not meet several required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Specifically, only I3 is satisfied (FDG-PET used). The study does not meet I4 (the sample is a single patient described as 'FTLD-like' rather than a clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease group), I5 (fewer than 6 participants in the patient group), I6 (no between-group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD group to controls), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). No exclusion criteria from the provided list apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the bvFTD meta-analysis. Inclusion criterion I4 is partially met (the sample includes 1 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient), but I3 (imaging modality) is not met—the study uses 123I-FP-CIT SPECT, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. I5 is not met: the bvFTD patient group has only n=1 (fewer than the required ≥6). I6 is not met: no between-group voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls is reported. I7 is not met: no whole-brain voxelwise results in MNI/Talairach space from a bvFTD group are reported. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria from the provided list were triggered. Therefore the paper must be excluded.
